name: T-72B3 / T-72 family
armament: 125 mm 2A46M-5 smoothbore with autoloader (fires 9M119 Refleks ATGM)
12.7 mm Kord on commander's remote/manual mount
protection: Steel/composite hull and turret with Kontakt-5 ERA (B3) or Relikt ERA (B3M) and rear slat/net screens. Game: hull and turret immune to all small-calibre and to 7.62x54R/12.7/14.5 mm (those only break optics, searchlights, external MGs and track pins). Kills need launchers: Javelin/NLAW top-attack, AT4/MAAWS/SMAW or RPG-7 PG-7V to side, rear or roof; frontal ERA defeats single-charge PG-7V.
visual_notes: Low rounded cast turret with brick-shaped Kontakt-5 ERA blocks in a chevron on the turret front and glacis; B3M adds Relikt boxes and side skirts with ERA
6 large road wheels per side with 3 small return rollers; rubber side skirts
Sosna-U gunner's sight box on the turret roof front-right, commander's cupola left
Unditching log and fuel drums on the rear hull; snorkel tube on the turret rear
2026 field look: welded roof 'cope cage' over the turret, anti-drone mesh/netting draped on frames, sometimes a full 'turtle' shed cover, EW jammer box on the turret, rubber mats over ERA
White tactical marks (Z, V, triangle) on Russian vehicles; Armenian/Azerbaijani/Serbian/Kazakh T-72s are older A/B/M1 versions without the B3 sight box

colour_schemes.name: Russian protective green with white Z/V/triangle ID marks

variants: T-72B3M / obr. 2016 (RUS, Africa Corps in Mali)
